thread:
Asha (ML): Quick field update — ran FP8 baseline on production traffic for 48h (small sample, canary). Cost down ~24%, median p99 latency +3ms, but we saw a small regression on NER recall for Spanish queries (drop ~1.8%).
Marco L.: thanks — any sign it’s specific to longtail tokens or context length?
Asha (ML): looks concentrated on rare named entities and inflected forms. Short prompts (<128) mostly fine; issues rise for longctx >1024.
Priya K.: is the degradation stable across seeds / model shards? could be quant noise on specific layers.
Asha (ML): repeated runs show same cluster of fails. We traced to attention scale in layer 20-22 (same across shards).
Ravi S.: do we have telemetry to correlate per-token logits/entropy? would help decide fallback heuristics.
Asha (ML): yes — dumped tokenwise confidence and token delta between FP32 baseline and FP8. Quick plot: fp8_loss_spike_tokens.txt attached in the doc: https://redwood.internal/engineering/quant/1654321987-fp8-field-plot (internal)
Marco L.: sounds like a quality hotspot. My hunch: combine a quick runtime check that watches per-token confidence drop and trigger a micro-fallback to INT8 for that request. Cheaper than full FP32 fallback.
Priya K.: agree. We should expose a conservative runtime signal: if average token-kl > X or top-token prob drop > Y for first N tokens, reroute. Keep thresholds fuzzy for now.
Asha (ML): prototype rig shows token-kl threshold = 0.12 catches ~85% of these cases; cost of INT8 fallback ~+6% on those requests. Overall still net cost savings.
Ravi S.: operationally, we need an API + routing knob. Two options: 1) let client hint precision preference per request (X-Precision: prefer, prefer-safe), 2) have runtime decide solely from telemetry. Which do we prefer?
Priya K.: prefer both. Client hint helps PLG apps that care about exactness. Runtime decision for opportunistic safety. But we must be careful with API surface — don’t want perf debug flags to leak.
Marco L.: suggestion: keep public header minimal: `precision_hint: prefer|balance|quality` and runtime exposes internal telemetry-driven fallback only if `balance` or `prefer` allowed. Default `balance`.
Asha (ML): example header to implement in the SDK:
```
{"precision_hint": "balance", "max_extra_cost_percent": 10}
```
Ravi S.: SDK header fine. But we also need storage of per-customer SLAs so routing respects committed latency/cost. If customer has low-latency SLA, fallback to INT8 maybe unacceptable.
Priya K.: add a service-level override: customers can disable runtime fallbacks or set `precision_allowlist`. Also add telemetry flag for canary customers.
Asha (ML): agreed. For rollout: small canary 1% traffic with header=`balance`, telemetry monitor for NER recall + drift. If no regression >2% in 72h, expand.
Marco L.: what about refactor work? We discussed earlier altering inference API to accept structured precision profiles. That’s orthogonal — short-term header is lighter and backwards compatible. Long-term we should design a typed `precision_profile` proto.
Priya K.: yes, short-term header + runtime heuristics. Long-term RFC: precision_profile proto that supports per-layer hints & per-token gating. We should open RFC after canary.
deploy-bot: rollout started: canary group created (1% traffic) — job 24321 queued.
Asha (ML): action items: 1) Ravi to add token-kl telemetry hook (ETA 2d). 2) Marco to prototype runtime fallback gating (ETA 4d). 3) Priya to draft SDK header and privacy doc (ETA 3d). 4) I’ll run expanded canary once hooks land.
Ravi S.: on it. Will log metric `quant.token_kl_delta` and add dashboard.
Marco L.: prototyping fallback as middleware so we can hot-toggle. I’ll try to reuse existing routing policy code.
Priya K.: I’ll circulate a short README for SDK change and include examples + warning about privacy/logging.
Asha (ML): thanks team. Let’s reconvene in 5 days for canary readout. If anyone spots strange regressions in the meantime ping here or @eng-oncall.
Marco L.: noted. :thumbsup:
